title: Gandhi and the Jailer: “I Demanded Swadeshi, Not Yerawada!”
summary: When handed a poorly crafted, blunt utility knife made in the prison workshop, Gandhi quipped: 'I advocated for fine Swadeshi craftsmanship, not crude Yerawada prison Swadeshi!'
keywords: Gandhi and the Jailer: “I Demanded Swadeshi, Not Yerawada!”
full_text:
In 1930, following the historic Salt March to Dandi, Mahatma Gandhi was imprisoned inside Yerawada Central Jail in Poona.

Despite being confined, Gandhi followed an exacting daily routine: spinning cotton, praying, and answering correspondence.

Needing a small utility knife to slice vegetables and open mail, Gandhi submitted a formal request to the British prison superintendent: "Please provide a small, domestically manufactured knife. It must be Swadeshi (Indian-made), not an imported foreign blade."

The superintendent ordered the prison workshop to craft a knife. An inexperienced convict hastily ground a scrap piece of rusted iron and attached a crude, wobbling wooden handle.

The superintendent proudly presented the finished tool to Gandhi in his cell.

Gandhi inspected the implement. The blade was crooked, pitted with rust, and so loose that applying pressure would likely dislodge the handle entirely.

Gandhi looked up at the superintendent with a wry smile:
"My dear Superintendent! Is this the pinnacle of British prison craftsmanship? This blade won't cut paper; it is far more likely to amputate my thumb!"

The superintendent replied defensively:
"Mr. Gandhi, you explicitly insisted upon Swadeshi! This knife was manufactured right here in India by our own prison workshop. It is one hundred percent Swadeshi!"

Gandhi laughed heartily and countered with razor-sharp wit:
"My dear sir! When I advocate for Swadeshi, I mean the exquisite, durable, and refined craftsmanship of Indian artisans! I certainly did not ask for crude, slapdash 'Yerawada Jail Swadeshi'! True Swadeshi embodies excellence, beauty, and precision, not carelessness masked as patriotism!"

The superintendent flushed with embarrassment, smiled sheepishly, and took back the crude knife.

The next morning, the prison authorities delivered a finely forged, beautifully polished utility knife crafted by an expert blacksmith. Even behind prison bars, Gandhi insisted that true self-reliance must never be an excuse for second-rate standards.
moral: Even within prison walls, Gandhi never compromised on quality, reminding us that national self-reliance must be synonymous with excellence, not shoddy work.
